content.user_title: Diagnose Pricing Gaps Before Changing Prices
content.value_statement: Pricing problems can come from weak demand evidence, misaligned billing units, or confusing tiers. This skill evaluates all three and recommends a focused next step.
actual_capabilities: Assess willingness-to-pay evidence, segment close rates, and discount behavior using a 0-100 scoring rubric.
Evaluate whether billing units track customer value and identify potential metric gaming.
Compare top-customer payments with median payments to investigate expansion misalignment.
Review tier differentiation, feature placement, and buyer distribution across packages.
Produce a three-surface report with scores, gaps, recommended actions, a triage decision, and a timeline.
Identify follow-up workflows for research, metric changes, packaging changes, audits, or quarterly review.
limitations: Requires current tiers, a billing metric, customer profiles, and discount policy; missing pricing setup routes to onboarding.
Does not collect willingness-to-pay research or invent missing close-rate data.
Scores follow qualitative rubrics and do not establish causal effects or guarantee revenue improvements.
Depends on a parent pricing workflow and referenced resources outside the reviewed single-file package.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Proposed Price Increase
use_cases.description: Separate missing willingness-to-pay evidence from genuine pricing opportunities before deciding whether to raise prices.

use_cases.title: Review Billing Metric Alignment
use_cases.description: Investigate whether high-value customers pay proportionately and whether the current billing unit limits expansion.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Tier Packaging Changes
use_cases.description: Compare tier clarity, feature placement, and buyer distribution to determine whether packaging needs attention before price levels.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Pricing Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose my pricing using the attached tiers, billing metric, customer profiles, and discount policy. Identify missing evidence before scoring.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review an existing pricing setup.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Discount Pressure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these segment close rates, discounts, and willingness-to-pay research. Score the three surfaces and explain whether more research should precede a price increase.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Metric and Packaging Problems
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these usage ratios, customer payment ratios, tier features, and buyer distributions. Distinguish billing misalignment from packaging problems and prioritize the gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare competing causes of revenue leakage.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pricing Triage Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate all supplied pricing evidence by customer profile. Explain each score, apply the triage matrix, name the next workflow, and estimate a timeline.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare an evidence-based cross-surface decision.

output_examples.input: Illustrative case: research is absent, discounts exceed policy, billing aligns with value, and tested tiers are clear.
output: Willingness to pay: low. Main gaps are missing research and discounts above policy.
Value metric: high. The supplied billing evidence aligns charges with customer value.
Packaging: high. Tested differentiation supports the existing tiers.
Triage: willingness-to-pay discovery before raising prices. Suggested timeline: about four weeks.

output_examples.input: Illustrative case: recent segment research and billing alignment are strong, but 60% of buyers choose a confusing bottom tier.
output: Willingness to pay: high. Recent segment evidence supports the review.
Value metric: high. Charges scale with customer success.
Packaging: low. Tier confusion and buyer concentration suggest a packaging problem.
Triage: packaging rebuild rather than a price change. Suggested timeline: about three weeks.

best_practices: Provide dated research and segment-level evidence alongside current tiers, billing units, customer profiles, and discount policy.
Explain each score using supplied evidence and distinguish missing data from observed problems.
Use the triage decision to prioritize investigation before implementing a material pricing change.
anti_patterns: Inventing willingness-to-pay percentiles, close rates, or customer usage data to complete the report.
Treating qualitative surface scores as precise forecasts of revenue or customer response.
Raising prices when the evidence indicates a billing metric or packaging problem.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: Provide current tiers and cadence, the billing unit, customer Pain Signal Profiles, and the discount policy.

faq.question: What does the report contain?
faq.answer: It includes three 0-100 scores, evidence-based gaps, recommended actions, a triage decision, a next workflow, and a timeline.

faq.question: Can it work without willingness-to-pay research?
faq.answer: It can use supplied close rates and discount evidence. It must identify missing research and must not invent willingness-to-pay numbers.

faq.question: Does it automatically change prices?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow produces diagnostic recommendations, not automatic billing changes or pricing-page deployment.

faq.question: Is it a standalone command?
faq.answer: No. It is marked as not user-invocable and is designed for routing from the parent pricing skill.

faq.question: What did the security review cover?
faq.answer: The review covered SKILL.md and adjudicated 23 static detections as false positives. Referenced resources and sibling skills were not reviewed.
